clue.text: Stubborn cur pinches one girl coming out

indicators.note: to pinch is to grip tightly, so the dog holds the other pieces inside it

parts.note: a cur is a mongrel dog, a hound
one is the Roman numeral I
a deb (debutante) is a young woman making her formal entry into society, her 'coming out'

explanation.surface: A badly behaved dog grabs a young society girl at her first ball.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone hidebound is rigidly set in their opinions, hence stubborn and unwilling to change.

clue.text: Neigh out of turn

indicators.note: letters that are out of order are jumbled, so the horse's call is rearranged

explanation.surface: A horse whinnies when it is not its turn to speak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of turn' reads as one idiom, but 'out of' is the anagram signal and 'turn' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To hinge on something is to turn or pivot on it, as a door swings on its pivot.

clue.text: Commissionaire wanting zero time to be at rest

indicators.note: wanting here means lacking, so one letter is dropped from the porter's title

parts.note: a commissionaire is a uniformed doorman at a hotel or theatre
zero looks like the letter O

explanation.surface: A hotel porter who has no time off just wants to rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Something dormant is inactive or sleeping, temporarily at rest rather than active.

clue.text: Attempt to restrict jerks from being like people

indicators.note: to restrict is to hem in, so the attempt surrounds the exercise

parts.note: a bid is an attempt
physical jerks are exercises, PE being physical education

explanation.surface: Someone tries to stop sudden twitches making them look like everyone else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jerks' suggests sudden movements; here physical jerks are school exercises, PE. 'from' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A biped is a two-legged creature, a being that walks upright on two feet as people do.

clue.text: Urged on in developing experience

indicators.note: something developing is changing shape, so the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Being pushed on helps someone build up their experience.
explanation.definitionFit: To undergo something is to experience or go through it, typically an ordeal or treatment.

clue.text: TV chap's taunt to Parisian that's entering place of vice

indicators.note: entering means going inside, so the taunt and French word sit within the den

parts.note: a den is a place of vice, as in a den of iniquity
to rag is to tease or taunt
a Parisian would say que for 'that'

explanation.surface: A television presenter mocks a Frenchman on his way into a seedy club.
explanation.walkthrough: TV here is short for transvestite, not television: the definition is a man dressed as a woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A drag queen is a male performer in women's clothing, so loosely a transvestite chap.

clue.text: Evasive about page's text

indicators.note: about means around, so the shy word goes round the page

parts.note: coy means reluctant to give details, evasive
P is the standard abbreviation for page

explanation.surface: Someone is cagey about what a page actually says.
explanation.definitionFit: Copy is the text of an article or advertisement, the written matter prepared for printing.

clue.text: Reduce the impact of American greeting that fool accepts

indicators.note: to accept is to take in, so the trick holds the other pieces

parts.note: to con someone is to fool them
hi is a greeting

explanation.surface: A trickster softens his blow by taking an American's friendly hello.
explanation.definitionFit: To cushion a blow is to soften it, lessening its force as a pad would.

clue.text: Church that eats sandwich gradually

indicators.note: to sandwich is to put between two layers, so the church goes between the two foods

parts.note: eats are food, here a pie and a meal
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A church congregation munches its sandwiches bit by bit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sandwich' looks like food but is the verb, and 'eats' is the old slang for food in general, here two dishes.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done piecemeal is done a bit at a time, gradually rather than all at once.

clue.text: I printed letters in bold

indicators.note: the letters of the words are taken and rearranged, as type is reset

explanation.surface: A typesetter puts a line in bold face.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bold' suggests bold type, a nice fit with 'printed', but it means brave.
explanation.definitionFit: Intrepid means fearless and adventurous, so bold in the sense of courageous.

clue.text: Jeans were part of the problem? On the contrary

indicators.note: part of says the letters are found within the words given

explanation.surface: Someone's jeans were to blame for their trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the contrary' turns the definition into the opposite of a problem: what solves it.
explanation.definitionFit: The opposite of a problem is its solution, so 'the problem? On the contrary' leads to a reply that solves it.

clue.text: Consideration about 5

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: 5 down is DRAG QUEEN; queen is ER, the Queen's royal cipher, so it reads DRAG plus ER

explanation.surface: A thought about the drag act.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference is to 5 down; read it as DRAG + ER, since queen = ER (Elizabeth Regina).
explanation.definitionFit: Regard is thought or attention given to something, as in having regard for others.

clue.text: Necessary to have sheets in colour

indicators.note: the sheets go in the colour, placed inside it

parts.note: red is a colour
a quire is a set of 24 or 25 sheets of paper

explanation.surface: Bed linen must be coloured.
explanation.definitionFit: Something required is needed or compulsory, hence necessary.

clue.text: Female protecting pussy from harm

indicators.note: protecting means surrounding as a guard, so the woman wraps round the cat

parts.note: she is a female pronoun
pussy is a pet name for a cat

explanation.surface: A woman shields her cat from injury.
explanation.definitionFit: To scathe is an old verb meaning to harm or injure, surviving in 'unscathed'.

clue.text: Coach horse has a lot of opportunity to go outside

indicators.note: to go outside means to surround, so the shortened word wraps the horse
a lot of means most but not all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a chance is an opportunity
an Arab is a breed of horse

explanation.surface: A coaching horse has plenty of chances to get out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a lot of' drops the last letter of the opportunity word; 'to go outside' wraps it round the horse. 'Coach' means a bus, not a trainer.
explanation.definitionFit: A charabanc is an old open motor coach used for day trips and outings.

clue.text: Thus no tailless vermin is designed for efficiency

parts.note: ergo is Latin for therefore, thus
taken as written

indicators.note: tailless means the last letter, the tail, is cut off

parts.note: mice are vermin

explanation.surface: So the rodents without tails are built to work better.
explanation.definitionFit: Ergonomic design arranges things for efficient, comfortable use by people in their work.

clue.text: Shrub that's unproductive when in flower

indicators.note: the thin word is placed in the river

parts.note: a flower is something that flows, a river: the Oder flows through Germany and Poland
a lean year or period is unproductive

explanation.surface: A shrub that bears nothing when it's blooming.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flower' is a river (it flows), the crossword trick; the Oder is a central European river.
explanation.definitionFit: Oleander is an evergreen Mediterranean shrub with poisonous leaves and showy flowers.

clue.text: Soccer bosses left in dark opening

parts.note: the FA, the Football Association, runs English soccer

indicators.note: left goes in the dark, placed inside it

parts.note: night is the dark

explanation.surface: Football bosses are kept uninformed about a vacancy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left in dark' suggests being uninformed; it places L inside NIGHT.
explanation.definitionFit: A fanlight is a small window above a door, a glazed opening to let in light.

clue.text: Young men like this girl?

parts.note: reads as lads fancying a girl, but means a girl who behaves like the lads, boisterous and hard-drinking

explanation.surface: Do the young men fancy this girl?
explanation.definitionFit: A ladette is a young woman who behaves in a loud, boozy way associated with lads.

clue.text: Matron's breaking into bar through window

indicators.note: breaking into pieces signals the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the 's counts as a letter S here, giving all seven letters

explanation.surface: A hospital matron is breaking into a pub through a window.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaking into bar' reads as burglary; 'breaking into' is the anagram signal and 'bar' starts the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A transom is a horizontal crossbar in a window or over a door.

clue.text: Marble man's about to receive Greeks' number one complaint

indicators.note: to receive is to take in, so the turned name holds the letter
about means turned round, so the name is read backwards

parts.note: Lord Elgin brought the Elgin Marbles from the Parthenon to London

indicators.note: the number one of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A man with a marble is about to get the chief Greek's grumble.
explanation.walkthrough: The Elgin Marbles, linked to the Greeks, are a long-running grievance, which helps the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A niggle is a small but persistent worry or complaint.

clue.text: Stuff with rum and butter

parts.note: grog is rum diluted with water, the old naval drink
a ram butts with its head, so it is a butter

explanation.surface: Stuffing made with rum and butter, like a Christmas pudding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stuff' means cloth, not a verb or filling; 'butter' is one who butts.
explanation.definitionFit: Grogram is a coarse fabric of silk mixed with mohair or wool, and stuff is an old word for cloth.

clue.text: Flower requiring poor drainage

indicators.note: poor here means badly made, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A plant that needs badly drained soil.
explanation.definitionFit: Gardenia is a shrub with fragrant white flowers, so its bloom is a flower.

clue.text: God's weapon chest

parts.note: Thor is the Norse god of thunder
ax (axe) is a weapon

explanation.surface: A box holding a god's weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chest' is a box in the surface but the body part here.
explanation.definitionFit: The thorax is the chest, the part of the body between neck and abdomen.

clue.text: 5's loom

definitions.meaning: 5 down is DRAG QUEEN; read as DRAG + ER (queen), one who drags, someone who tows
to loom is to rise up high over something

explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference reads 5 down as DRAG + ER, since queen = ER, giving one who drags.
explanation.definitionFit: A tower rises high, and to tower is to loom; one who tows is also a dragger.

clue.text: Gas and chatter away with Jack

indicators.note: away with means remove, so the letter is taken out

parts.note: jargon originally meant meaningless chatter
J is short for Jack in cards

explanation.surface: Someone talks and chatters on with a sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: Argon is an inert gas, a noble gas making up about one per cent of air.

clue.text: Forbid Scottish cap made from fowl

parts.note: to ban is to forbid
a tam (tam-o'-shanter) is a Scottish cap

explanation.surface: Ban a Scottish hat made from feathers.
explanation.definitionFit: A bantam is a small breed of domestic chicken, a fowl.

clue.text: Wise restriction on vessel removing waste

indicators.note: a restriction hems something in, so the wise word wraps the jug

parts.note: sage means wise
a ewer is a large jug, a vessel

explanation.surface: Wise limits on a ship getting rid of rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: Sewerage is the system of drains for carrying off waste and sewage.

clue.text: Top marks received by one in a suit

indicators.note: received by means taken inside, so the card holds the money

parts.note: the ace is the one in a suit of playing cards
M is short for marks, the old German currency

explanation.surface: Good grades for someone in a business suit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one in a suit' suggests a businessman, but it is the ace in a suit of cards.
explanation.definitionFit: The acme is the peak or highest point, the top of achievement.

clue.text: Photographer arrived and managed to snap Madonna being heartless

parts.note: came means arrived

indicators.note: to snap is to catch, so the run grips the letters

parts.note: ran means managed

indicators.note: heartless means the inner letters go, leaving just the ends

explanation.surface: A photographer shows up and manages to snap a cold-hearted pop star.
explanation.walkthrough: 'snap' suggests a photograph, but it means catch hold of: RAN snaps MA, the outside of Madonna.
explanation.definitionFit: A cameraman operates a camera, for film or television, so is a kind of photographer.
